keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Human demonstrations
keywords.about: Policies are cloned from human video, motion and force-feedback demonstrations, including few-shot driving.

keywords.name: LLM Agents
keywords.about: Agents are benchmarked on tool use, computer use, scientific problems and safety compliance.

keywords.name: Agentic RL
keywords.about: Long-horizon agent training with outcome rewards, credit assignment and self-distillation.

keywords.name: Robot Manipulation
keywords.about: Dexterous hands, humanoids and mobile robots learn contact-rich manipulation from tactile and force feedback.

keywords.name: World Models
keywords.about: Action-conditioned world models predict futures for driving, humanoid control and robot planning.

keywords.name: Vision-Language-Action Models
keywords.about: Deployment-time adaptation and improvement of vision-language-action robot policies.

keywords.name: Mixture-of-Experts
keywords.about: MoE routing, dense-to-MoE conversion and LoRA experts allocate compute unevenly across layers.

keywords.name: Activation Steering
keywords.about: Probing and steering hidden states to surface safety-relevant reasoning and routing representations.

keywords.name: LLM-as-a-Judge
keywords.about: Meta-evaluating judge models and metrics for factual retrieval, ranking and multilingual generation.

keywords.name: On-Policy Distillation
keywords.about: Students train on their own rollouts with token-level credit from a teacher model.

keywords.name: Agent Harnesses
keywords.about: Verifiable harnesses and runtimes let agents extend, improve and gate their own execution.

keywords.name: RLVR
keywords.about: Verifier rewards train reasoning models, with reward hacking diagnosed and corrected.

keywords.name: Thompson Sampling
keywords.about: Regret bounds and convergence rates for Thompson sampling in games and Gaussian-process optimization.

themes.name: Embodied robot learning and vision-language-action policies
themes.summary: These papers develop embodied robot learning and vision-language-action policies, spanning agentic robot orchestration, physical-time policy memory, autonomous driving VLA, humanoid loco-manipulation, visual heading, wearable gait estimation, active perception, dexterous tracking, onboard spacecraft learning, and collective manipulation. They differ by focusing on memory dynamics, datasets, task-specific estimators, or policy generalization across embodiments.

themes.name: Trustworthy AI and prompt-injection safety
themes.summary: These papers study trustworthy AI and prompt-injection safety through robustness benchmarks, adversarial assurance limits, anomaly detection, LoRA concept discovery, cyber attack-defense, pluralistic preference alignment, memorization detection, theory-of-mind certification, and channel-aware prompt-injection defense. They differ in threat models and evaluation targets, from static decision models to live agent combat.

themes.name: LLM reasoning, planning, and verifiable-reward optimization
themes.summary: These papers work on LLM reasoning, planning, and verifiable-reward optimization, including long-horizon harness engineering, reward hacking in instruction following, inverse reasoning from answer-only data, event prediction, coding agents for visual generation, RL prompt optimization, tool discovery, continuous flow verifier rewards, item-level prompt transitions, and contextual credit assignment. They differ in whether they benchmark, diagnose, or optimize reasoning and planning pipelines.

themes.name: Benchmark and multimodal evaluation studies
themes.summary: These papers introduce benchmarks and meta-evaluation studies for multimodal and LLM evaluation, covering emotion-conditioned tool-calling agents, VLM physiological measurement, Chatbot Arena choice axioms, aerial video understanding, spatial reasoning, style-personalized generation metrics, evaluation setup reliability, user-centric benchmark auditing, jailbreak evaluation, and persona information use. They differ in evaluation objects and whether they audit, meta-evaluate, or propose new diagnostic games.

themes.name: Video generation and action-conditioned world models
themes.summary: These papers focus on video generation and action-conditioned world models, including agentic video generation, visual motion to action, actuator residual world models, action-manifold jets, world-memory benchmarking, geometric horizon models, LiDAR world models, drift-diffusion prediction, slot-memory long-horizon generation, and audio-driven avatar video. They differ in spatial memory, action conditioning, and generation modality.

themes.name: Reinforcement-learning algorithms and theory
themes.summary: These papers develop reinforcement-learning algorithms and theory for long-horizon agents, Thompson sampling in zero-sum games, delayed and censored labels, regret matching, online assignment, active inference, strategic queuing, multiagent cooperation, autonomous driving comparison, and mode collapse. They differ in theoretical guarantees, feedback models, and application settings.

themes.name: Autonomous LLM agents for science and self-improvement
themes.summary: These papers examine autonomous LLM agents for science and self-improvement, including theoretical physics problem solving, agentic scientific co-discovery, conjecture-guided discovery, first-principles anyon identification, open research benchmarks, program-generation harness optimization, personalized skill learning, recursive capability composition, video-understanding harness self-improvement, and gating scientific workflow releases. They differ in scientific domain and self-improvement mechanism.

themes.name: Time-series and tabular foundation models
themes.summary: These papers address time-series and tabular foundation models, covering forecast-grounded time-series language models, streaming telemetry fault diagnosis, forest classification, novelty detection, next-location prediction, wearable activity recognition, IMU representation benchmarking, sequence conformal prediction, typed decision models on tabular data, and test-time forecasting with recurrent depth. They differ in modality, task, and whether they pretrain, benchmark, or calibrate predictions.

themes.name: 3D reconstruction and Gaussian splatting
themes.summary: These papers study 3D reconstruction and Gaussian splatting, including under-ice robotic perception, source-aware lighting estimation, spacecraft pose tracking, sparse panorama reconstruction, hyperspectral unmixing, Gaussian splatting compression, single-image garment reconstruction, long-horizon geometry memory, microfacet neural SDFs, and queryable 3D-anchored scene generation. They differ in reconstruction target, representation, and evaluation benchmark.

themes.name: Graph neural networks and relational learning
themes.summary: These papers develop graph neural networks and relational learning methods for network-linked regression, graph coarsening in MAX-CUT, GNNs in graph databases, wildfire spread prediction, topology-pass scheduling, size generalization, graph transformer attention, dynamic graph world modelling, explainable recommendation, and heterogeneous circuit variational autoencoding. They differ in graph type, task, and theoretical or application focus.

themes.name: Physics-informed neural operators and simulation
themes.summary: These papers develop physics-informed and differentiable simulation methods across domains, including multi-fidelity surrogates for supercavity geometry, differentiable EPR and contact-dynamics simulators, and neural operators for stochastic Volterra equations and self-interference cancellation. They differ in technique: some embed physical laws or constraints directly (SKG, physics-informed weak regression, diffusion-regularized full waveform inversion), while others focus on structured or differentiable architectures for learning solution operators.

themes.name: Efficient inference, quantization, and speculative decoding
themes.summary: These papers improve LLM inference efficiency through architectural and algorithmic changes such as sparse attention (JSSA), structured pruning (LayerTrim), dense-to-MoE conversion (Spectral-MoE), KV-cache quantization (PN-Mix), external memory (Titan-Llama), and parallelism trade-offs. They differ in the bottleneck they target: attention sparsity, MLP/expert trimming, low-bit key cache precision, tokenization latency, or throughput-latency balance.

highlights.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
highlights.authors: Weijie Wang, Haomin Zhang, Ye Li et al.
highlights.theme: Video generation and action-conditioned world models
highlights.why: Introduces a world-state memory framework that substantially improves cross-shot spatial and temporal consistency for agentic video generation, with strong empirical gains across multiple generators.
highlights.key_result: Across four video generators, ATAS improves all reported cross-shot consistency measures and achieves the highest aggregate benchmark score for each backbone, and it also outperforms the compared agents and 3D-guided methods on target-image spatial revisit, reaching 15.968 PSNR_C, 0.385 SSIM_C, and 0.284 LPIPS_C. It leads three event-recapture criteria — event identity (0.750), temporal order (0.688), and viewpoint realization (0.650) — and receives the highest human ratings on all six criteria.

highlights.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
highlights.authors: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu et al.
highlights.why: Proposes a scalable post-training framework using synthetic environments and PPO to teach game control to computer-use agents, demonstrating a viable path beyond demonstration-based learning.
highlights.key_result: Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively, and Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld.

highlights.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
highlights.authors: Huining Yuan, Xiangmin Yi, Zelai Xu et al.
highlights.why: Reframes agent distillation as aligning semantic actions rather than token probabilities, offering a principled and practical distillation objective for black-box teachers.
highlights.key_result: ActionOPD, an action-level on-policy distillation method, trains Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B students with two teachers on diverse curated tool-use tasks, yielding average gains of 3.3--6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks while requiring only generation access to a black-box teacher.
evidence: Training Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with two teachers on diverse, curated tool-use tasks yields average gains of 3.3--6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks.

In practice, ActionOPD samples actions from the teacher and responses from the current student policy, rewarding student responses according to their semantic agreement with teacher actions. It requires only generation access to a black-box teacher, not teacher token probabilities or tokenizer alignment.

highlights.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
highlights.authors: Linhao Zhong, Bozhen Fang, Xuehao Wang et al.
highlights.theme: LLM reasoning, planning, and verifiable-reward optimization
highlights.why: A large-scale controlled comparison revealing limited and unstable gains from self-distillation methods over GRPO, providing a valuable negative result.
highlights.key_result: Comparing ten representative self-distillation methods against GRPO across four agent benchmarks and three model sizes, the study finds that only PCSD (54.26, +4.58 points) and AgentOPSD (51.34, +1.66 points) exceed GRPO's twelve-setting mean of 49.68, with no method consistently outperforming GRPO across settings. The study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours.
evidence: To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods.

All ten alternatives improve on GRPO in some settings, but only a minority retain an advantage in aggregate. Only PCSD (54.26, +4.58 points) and AgentOPSD (51.34, +1.66 points) exceed GRPO's twelve-setting mean of 49.68; the other eight alternatives fall below it.

Gains over GRPO remain setting-dependent, with no method uniformly superior; strong final results can conceal unstable training, and additional computation does not consistently improve performance.

highlights.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following
highlights.authors: Sangyeon Yoon, Wooseok Seo, Hamish Ivison et al.
highlights.theme: LLM reasoning, planning, and verifiable-reward optimization
highlights.why: Identifies and corrects reward hacking in verifiable instruction following with a calibrated likelihood bonus, improving both constraint satisfaction and response quality.
highlights.key_result: Across models ranging from 1.7B to 8B in reasoning and non-reasoning modes, CaLIF improves constraint satisfaction on IFBench while maintaining response quality near or above pre-RL levels; on average across five model configurations, IF-RLVR increases Constraint Satisfaction from 26.98 to 44.93 but reduces Response Quality from 4.51 to 2.96, while CaLIF improves both metrics to 34.64 and 4.59.

highlights.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
highlights.authors: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal et al.
highlights.theme: Autonomous LLM agents for science and self-improvement
highlights.why: A carefully curated set of unpublished theoretical physics problems showing frontier agents can solve them near-perfectly, raising important questions about memorization and capability.
highlights.key_result: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem.
evidence: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. highlights.title: Limits of Statistical Assurance for Embodied and Agentic AI under Adaptive Adversaries
highlights.why: Gives a formal characterization of unavoidable post-certification risk under adaptive adversaries, with empirical validation in embodied and tool-use settings.

highlights.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
highlights.authors: Soovadeep Bakshi, Apurba Bose, Aishwarya Bose et al.
highlights.why: Provides rigorous evidence that Bradley-Terry rankings mis-rank near-copies in Chatbot Arena, challenging a widely used evaluation paradigm.
highlights.key_result: On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley--Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later gives consistent multipliers, and the effect survives alternative tie treatments, prompt subsets and topics, and timing checks. A correction with four to six parameters predicts held-out votes better than Bradley--Terry and than models with hundreds of parameters, mostly by modelling ties; frozen and carried to new releases in a test fixed in advance, its gains are concentrated in ties, and better head-to-head odds are not established.

news.title: Amp puts AI agents to work beyond code with OpenAI models
news.summary: Amp is building a frontier AI agent using OpenAI models, which account for the majority of tokens used in Amp, and launched a Sign in with ChatGPT integration that gives users access to more tokens and models including GPT-6 Astra. Amp announced Puck, a conversational assistant built into Amp, with Calling Puck powered by GPT-Live-1 and an Ultrafast mode tested with GPT-6 Astra; Quinn Slack cites users consuming 10 billion tokens a week and Amp's 20-person team using agents for marketing and design work.

news.title: SentinelOne cuts malware analysis from weeks to hours
news.summary: SentinelOne uses OpenAI Daybreak for cybersecurity work to reverse-engineer malware, which it says now produces human-level reverse-engineering output in roughly eight hours, down from four to six weeks for a top security researcher. According to Chief AI Officer Gregor Stewart, the faster analysis lets researchers investigate more samples and compare findings across them, while human accountability is retained for decisions such as architecture changes.

news.title: How Third Moment Research runs 10,000 agents for 36+ hours
How Block is building AI-powered security with OpenAI technology
news.summary: Block is using OpenAI Daybreak and the OpenAI Defense Factory across its security workflows, including replaying a proposed detection change against seven months of production telemetry in under an hour, going from a high-level vulnerability to an automated proposed patch in 18 minutes, and completing ~1,100 analyst-hours of investigation per quarter. Block reports ~600 analyst-hours per quarter handed back through false-positive triage, a 50% boost to triage throughput, a 50% increase in intelligence gathering and investigations, and a new autonomous hunting capability, with a human validating every result.

news.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
news.summary: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore fine-tuned Google's lightweight Gemma model on local scam conversations to build a privacy-preserving, on-device scam detection model, presented at Singapore International Cyber Week (SICW 2026). The text states scams make up over half of Singapore's reported crimes and more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019, with such scams accounting for up to 80% of all losses; the two-stage pipeline runs a lightweight classifier followed by in-context analysis with the fine-tuned Gemma model.

news.title: Research@ 2026: 10 ways we're amplifying human ingenuity
news.summary: At its Research@ event, Google Research listed 10 highlights including expanded early access to Google Earth AI, integration of Google Dataset Search for querying more than 100 million public datasets, and capabilities powered by over 70 geospatial tools. Google.org is providing $10 million in funding for crisis resilience and public health, including $2 million to The Milken Institute, and a multi-agent orchestrator helped researchers apply a fluid-mechanics inverse design methodology to urinary catheter designs that in simulation were better at preventing bacterial infections.

news.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
news.summary: Google Research published a technical report on its Geospatial Reasoning agent, presenting systematic evaluations across four benchmarks including two new ones, GeoKTools and GeoExpertQueries. Partner testing involved the WHO Regional Office for Africa, People in Need, GiveDirectly, the Milken Institute and WPP for workflows such as disease outbreak investigations, disaster preparedness and clean energy screening, and early access is expanding via an experimental deep research update for Ask Google Earth and an agent-to-agent API.

news.title: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review
news.summary: Google Research publicly released Deep Review, an agentic system for technical verification of documents, after deployments across 16,000+ opt-in submissions at STOC 2026, ICML 2026, NeurIPS 2026 and ICLR 2027. Every user receives two complimentary document reviews per week, with higher limits and API access via a Gemini API key; initial input support covers PDFs and plain text, and uploaded documents are stored for one year and never used to train, fine-tune or improve Google models. The post cites over 74,000 submissions to ICLR, NeurIPS and ICML this year, up from approximately 45,000 in 2025, 32,000 in 2024 and 23,000 in 2023.

news.title: Preparing for the 2026 US midterms
news.summary: Anthropic described election safeguards ahead of the 2026 US midterms, based on an Anthropic Insights analysis of 250,000 conversations over a one-week period; in US Claude.ai conversations, politics/public policy/social issues accounted for about 5.75%, elections or voting about 0.51%, requests for whom or what to vote for about 0.01%, and election integrity policy violations about 0.002%. Claude will draw official voting information from Democracy Works for US users and show up-to-date election results, alongside the existing TurboVote banner.

news.title: Singapore office and government MOU
news.summary: Anthropic opened a Singapore office, its fifth in the Asia-Pacific region, and signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Singapore Ministry of Digital Development and Information covering AI safety, security, model evaluation, AI adoption research and responsible adoption. The post states Singapore ranks second of 121 countries in Claude.ai usage relative to population, at nearly six times what its size alone would predict, and that more than 1,500 engineers and technical staff at GovTech Singapore have adopted Claude Code.

news.title: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem
news.summary: NVIDIA announced planned investments in Boltz, Foresight, Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane as part of its UK startup ecosystem investments, alongside a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the UK's agentic safety and security research. The post also cites Fuse Energy moving customer AI onto infrastructure built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra for over 450,000 UK households, Locai Labs releasing Nemotron-Personas-UK with one million synthetic personas, and Danaher's AI-powered autonomous lab designed for up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents.

news.title: European Cities Deploy NVIDIA-Powered AI Agents to Run Smarter Urban Operations
news.summary: NVIDIA reported that cities and partners across the EMEA region are using its accelerated computing, Cosmos and Nemotron models plus the Metropolis VSS blueprint to build physical AI agents and digital twins, with projects spanning Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden and the UK. In France's Côte-d'Or, agents across more than 500 public buildings cut document search time from weeks to minutes and reduced total operating costs by 10%, targeting 30% at scale; in Italy's Milan region, deployment starts with Cinisello Balsamo and plans expansion to four additional municipalities.

news.title: Optimizing Agent Reliability and Tool Calling Efficiency for Chip Design Using NVIDIA NeMo Gym
news.summary: NVIDIA describes how Siemens EDA used the NeMo Gym agentic evaluation environment to improve the Siemens Fuse EDA AI Agent for Liberty file generation in standard-cell characterization, increasing the composite verification score from approximately 55% to ~95% while cutting agent turns by 66%. Agent turns decreased from 155 to 53 and output tokens fell from approximately 81K to 29K after refining skills and Model Context Protocol tool descriptions based on verifier diagnostics; a domain-specific verifier assigns zero reward if any of its five gates fails.

news.title: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
news.summary: Hugging Face introduced HiRO-ACEv2, an update to the HiRO-ACE climate emulator whose HiROv2 downscaling model predicts several high-resolution fields at once and generates global 3 km climate data at about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD. The text reports HiROv2 matches target high-resolution statistics to within 3% even for events occurring once in a million data points, that producing global high-resolution data costs roughly 300 times less than X-SHiELD with regional savings more than a hundred times greater, and that a streamlined version could be more than ten times faster.

news.title: Build self-improving document processing using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS describes building a self-improving agentic intelligent document processing system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, in which eight specialized agents collaborate across two graph-based workflows, with deployment often in under 20 minutes. The post cites IDC research that document challenges cost organizations $19,732 per information worker annually and reduce productivity by 21.3%, that staff can spend up to 30% of their time on document tasks, and that manual data entry error rates range from 1–4%.

news.title: Generate presentations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS describes using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the Strands Agents framework to build a supervisor agent that generates PowerPoint presentations, completing in under 90 seconds in internal testing. The solution uses Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6, Amazon Titan Text Embeddings v2 and Stability AI Stable Image Inpaint, exposes generate_pptx and generate_summary tools via a REST API built with .NET 8 minimal APIs, and stores vectors in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.

news.title: How Tamnoon built AI-powered cloud security remediation with Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Tamnoon built Tami, an agentic cloud remediation orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock, which autonomously investigates findings from CNAPP and cloud-native sources and generates fixes with guardrails. The post states the approach drove an over 90 percent reduction in critical cloud exposure in 90 days with zero production issues, and that four specialized agents handle distinct phases of the remediation pipeline.

news.title: Deploy and evaluate models with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
news.summary: AWS shows how to deploy a pretrained model from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, run a repeatable performance test using the SageMaker Python SDK, and delete the endpoint. The post notes that in 2026 SageMaker JumpStart added pre-configured endpoint deployment options optimized for priorities such as low cost, low latency or general-purpose workloads, and single-click deployment from Hugging Face model discovery.

themes.summary: 这些论文研究 3D 重建和高斯溅射，包括冰下机器人感知、源感知光照估计、航天器姿态跟踪、稀疏全景重建、高光谱解混、高斯溅射压缩、单图像服装重建、长时程几何记忆、微面元神经 SDF 以及可查询的 3D 锚定场景生成。它们的不同之处在于重建目标、表示和评估基准。

themes.name: 图神经网络与关系学习
themes.summary: 这些论文发展用于网络链接回归、MAX-CUT 中的图粗化、图数据库中的 GNN、野火蔓延预测、拓扑传递调度、规模泛化、图 transformer 注意力、动态图世界建模、可解释推荐和异质电路变分自编码的图神经网络和关系学习方法。它们的不同之处在于图类型、任务以及理论或应用重点。

themes.name: 物理信息神经算子与仿真
themes.summary: 这些论文发展跨领域的物理信息和可微分仿真方法，包括超空泡几何的多保真代理模型、可微分 EPR 和接触动力学仿真器，以及用于随机 Volterra 方程和自干扰消除的神经算子。它们的技术不同：有些直接嵌入物理定律或约束（SKG、物理信息弱回归、扩散正则化全波形反演），而另一些侧重于用于学习解算子的结构化或可微分架构。

themes.name: 高效推理、量化与投机解码
themes.summary: 这些论文通过架构和算法改进提高 LLM 推理效率，例如稀疏注意力（JSSA）、结构化剪枝（LayerTrim）、稠密到 MoE 转换（Spectral-MoE）、KV 缓存量化（PN-Mix）、外部记忆（Titan-Llama）以及并行权衡。它们的不同之处在于针对的瓶颈：注意力稀疏性、MLP/专家修剪、低位键缓存精度、分词延迟或吞吐量-延迟平衡。

highlights.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
highlights.authors: Weijie Wang, Haomin Zhang, Ye Li et al.
highlights.theme: Video generation and action-conditioned world models
highlights.why: 引入了一种世界状态记忆框架，大幅提升了智能体视频生成中的跨镜头空间和时间一致性，并在多个生成器上取得了显著的实证收益。
highlights.key_result: 在四个视频生成器上，ATAS 改善了所有报告的跨镜头一致性指标，并在每个骨干网络上取得了最高的聚合基准分数；同时，在目标图像空间重访方面，它也优于所比较的 agent 和 3D 引导方法，达到 15.968 PSNR_C、0.385 SSIM_C 和 0.284 LPIPS_C。它在三项事件重捕标准上领先——事件身份（0.750）、时间顺序（0.688）和视角实现（0.650）——并且在全部六项标准上获得了最高的人类评价。
evidence: Across four video generators, ATAS improves all reported cross-shot consistency measures and achieves the highest aggregate benchmark score for each backbone.
It also outperforms the compared agents and 3D-guided methods on target-image spatial revisit, leads three event-recapture criteria, and receives the highest human ratings on all six criteria.

ATAS reaches 15.968 PSNR_C, 0.385 SSIM_C, and 0.284 LPIPS_C, outperforming the compared multi-shot and 3D-guided methods (Tab. ). In Tab. , it leads event identity (0.750), temporal order (0.688), and viewpoint realization (0.650), ties ReCA on character and object consistency (0.917), and remains slightly lower on action-state preservation (0.688 versus 0.700).

highlights.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
highlights.authors: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu et al.
highlights.why: 提出了一种可扩展的后训练框架，利用合成环境和 PPO 教会计算机使用智能体进行游戏控制，展示了一条超越基于示范学习的可行路径。
highlights.key_result: Player-1-9B 和 Player-1-35B-A3B 相对于其 SFT 策略，在 MineDojo-300 上的成功率分别提高了 27.8 和 17.7 个百分点；Player-1-9B 的成功率达到 38.33%，而最强评估基线的成功率为 12.63%；此外，在 ViZDoom-10 和 GameWorld 上还相较 SFT 有进一步提升。
evidence: The resulting Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively. Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld.

On MineDojo-300, Player-1-9B improves from 10.54% success after SFT to 38.33%, exceeding the strongest evaluated external baseline at 12.63% under our evaluation protocol. The same policy also improves on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld, both outside the RL training suite.

We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience advances game-control capabilities beyond supervised demonstrations: Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B gain 27.8 and 17.7 pp in MineDojo-300 success, respectively, with further gains on ViZDoom and GameWorld outside the RL training suite.

highlights.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
highlights.authors: Huining Yuan, Xiangmin Yi, Zelai Xu et al.
highlights.why: 将智能体蒸馏重新定义为对齐语义动作而非 token 概率，为黑盒教师提供了一种有原则且实用的蒸馏目标。
highlights.key_result: ActionOPD 是一种动作级在线策略蒸馏方法，在多样化的精选工具使用任务上使用两位教师训练 Qwen3-4B 和 Qwen3-8B 学生模型，在四个分布外基准上平均提升 3.3--6.9 个百分点，同时仅需对黑盒教师的生成访问权限。
evidence: Training Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with two teachers on diverse, curated tool-use tasks yields average gains of 3.3--6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks.

In practice, ActionOPD samples actions from the teacher and responses from the current student policy, rewarding student responses according to their semantic agreement with teacher actions. It requires only generation access to a black-box teacher, not teacher token probabilities or tokenizer alignment.

highlights.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
highlights.authors: Linhao Zhong, Bozhen Fang, Xuehao Wang et al.
highlights.theme: LLM reasoning, planning, and verifiable-reward optimization
highlights.why: 一项大规模受控比较揭示了自蒸馏方法相对于 GRPO 的收益有限且不稳定，提供了一项有价值的负面结果。
highlights.key_result: 在四个智能体基准和三种模型规模上，将十种代表性自蒸馏方法与 GRPO 进行比较，研究发现只有 PCSD（54.26，+4.58 分）和 AgentOPSD（51.34，+1.66 分）超过了 GRPO 在十二种设置下的均值 49.68，且没有一种方法能在各设置中一致地优于 GRPO。该研究包含 132 次训练运行，总计记录 12,124.4 个 H800 GPU 小时。
evidence: To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods.

All ten alternatives improve on GRPO in some settings, but only a minority retain an advantage in aggregate. Only PCSD (54.26, +4.58 points) and AgentOPSD (51.34, +1.66 points) exceed GRPO's twelve-setting mean of 49.68; the other eight alternatives fall below it.

We benchmark ten representative self-distillation methods against GRPO across four agent benchmarks and three model sizes. Gains over GRPO remain setting-dependent, with no method uniformly superior; strong final results can conceal unstable training, and additional computation does not consistently improve performance.

highlights.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following
highlights.authors: Sangyeon Yoon, Wooseok Seo, Hamish Ivison et al.
highlights.theme: LLM reasoning, planning, and verifiable-reward optimization
highlights.why: 识别并纠正了可验证指令遵循中的奖励黑客行为，通过校准似然奖励，同时提升约束满足度和响应质量。
highlights.key_result: 在从 1.7B 到 8B、推理和非推理模式的模型上，CaLIF 在 IFBench 上提升了约束满足度，同时将响应质量维持在预 RL 水平附近或之上；在五种模型配置的平均结果中，IF-RLVR 将约束满足度从 26.98 提高到 44.93，但将响应质量从 4.51 降低到 2.96，而 CaLIF 将这两项指标分别改善至 34.64 和 4.59。
evidence: On average across these configurations, IF-RLVR increases Constraint Satisfaction (0--100 scale) from 26.98 to 44.93 but reduces Response Quality (1--10 scale) from 4.51 to 2.96, while CaLIF improves both metrics to 34.64 and 4.59, respectively.
Across models ranging from 1.7B to 8B in reasoning and non-reasoning modes, CaLIF improves constraint satisfaction on IFBench while maintaining response quality near or above pre-RL levels.
It also outperforms corresponding base policies in 40 of 45 model--metric comparisons across three rubric-based instruction-following benchmarks, demonstrating gains beyond training verifiers.

highlights.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
highlights.authors: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal et al.
highlights.theme: Autonomous LLM agents for science and self-improvement
highlights.why: 一组精心整理的未发表理论物理问题显示前沿智能体能够近乎完美地解决这些问题，引发了关于记忆化和能力的重要问题。
highlights.key_result: 我们提供了一套 50 道未发表的研究级理论物理问题，带有可验证答案。在获得现实环境中的工具（包括检索文献和编写数值与符号计算脚本的能力）时，表现最佳的智能体——在 Codex 中调用的 GPT-6-Astra——以 98% 的近乎完美准确率获得最终答案，每道题平均成本低于 USD 3。
evidence: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem.

highlights.title: Limits of Statistical Assurance for Embodied and Agentic AI under Adaptive Adversaries
highlights.why: 给出了自适应对手下不可避免的认证后风险的形式化刻画，并在具身和工具使用场景中进行了实证验证。
highlights.key_result: 一个在可观测、不可撤销的认证之前保留完整观测规律、并在之后保留干预访问权限的对手，在 n 次试验中可获得 v E[(n-S_0)_+] 的认证后事件期望值。在实验中，切换在 36 次认证后 RoCo 片段中有 34 次产生指令分离违规；预注册的随机 AgentDojo 试验估计，每次四任务延续平均增加 1.98 次安全违规（95% 区间 [1.67,2.29]）。
evidence: An adversary that preserves the complete observation law until observable, irrevocable certification and retains intervention access afterward attains v E[(n-S_0)_+] expected post-certification events over n trials. Here v is the active event probability and S_0 the unattacked certification time.
In simulated RoCo collaboration, switching produces commanded-separation violations in 34 of 36 post-certification episodes.
Preregistered randomized AgentDojo trials estimate 1.98 additional security violations per four-task continuation (95% interval [1.67,2.29]).

highlights.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
highlights.authors: Soovadeep Bakshi, Apurba Bose, Aishwarya Bose et al.
highlights.why: 提供了严格的证据，表明 Bradley-Terry 排名在 Chatbot Arena 中对近似副本的排序有误，挑战了广泛使用的评估范式。
highlights.key_result: 在 1.8 million 次 Arena 投票中，同一模型不同版本之间的投票决定性比 Bradley--Terry 预测的高 1.37 倍，同一代不同规模之间高 1.26 倍，同一实验室不同模型之间高 1.12 倍；一年后的版本给出了一致的乘数，且这一效应在替代平局处理、提示子集和主题以及时间检验下仍然存在。一个具有四到六个参数的校正模型对保留投票的预测优于 Bradley--Terry 和数百参数的模型，主要通过对平局的建模；在预先固定的测试中冻结并应用于新版本，其收益集中在平局上，且未建立更优的正面交锋赔率。
evidence: On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley--Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later gives consistent multipliers, and the effect survives alternative tie treatments, prompt subsets and topics, and timing checks.

A correction with four to six parameters predicts held-out votes better than Bradley--Terry and than models with hundreds of parameters, mostly by modelling ties; frozen and carried to new releases in a test fixed in advance, its gains are concentrated in ties, and better head-to-head odds are not established.

How Block is building AI-powered security with OpenAI technology

news.title: Research@ 2026: 10 ways we're amplifying human ingenuity

news.title: Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review
news.summary: Google Research 公开发布了 Deep Review，一个用于文档技术验证的智能体系统，此前已在 STOC 2026、ICML 2026、NeurIPS 2026 和 ICLR 2027 的 16,000+ 份自愿提交上部署。每位用户每周可获得两次免费文档评审，通过 Gemini API 密钥可获得更高限额和 API 访问；初始输入支持 PDF 和纯文本，上传的文档存储一年，绝不用于训练、微调或改进 Google 模型。文章引用称，今年 ICLR、NeurIPS 和 ICML 的提交量超过 74,000 份，高于 2025 年的约 45,000 份、2024 年的 32,000 份和 2023 年的 23,000 份。

news.summary: Anthropic 在新加坡开设了办事处，这是其在亚太地区的第五个办事处，并与新加坡数字发展与信息部签署了谅解备忘录，涵盖 AI 安全、安全、模型评估、AI 采用研究和负责任采用。文章称，新加坡在 121 个国家中按人口比例计算的 Claude.ai 使用量排名第二，接近其规模本身所预测的六倍，并且 GovTech Singapore 已有超过 1,500 名工程师和技术人员采用了 Claude Code。

news.title: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem

news.title: Optimizing Agent Reliability and Tool Calling Efficiency for Chip Design Using NVIDIA NeMo Gym

news.title: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
news.summary: Hugging Face 推出了 HiRO-ACEv2，这是 HiRO-ACE 气候模拟器的更新版本，其 HiROv2 降尺度模型同时预测多个高分辨率场，并以约 X-SHiELD 的 1/300th 成本生成全球 3 km 气候数据。文章报告称，HiROv2 能将目标高分辨率统计量匹配到 3% 以内，即使对于每 million 个数据点才出现一次的事件也是如此；生成全球高分辨率数据的成本比 X-SHiELD 大约低 300 倍，区域节省甚至超过一百倍；精简版本还可能快十倍以上。

news.title: Build self-improving document processing using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS 描述了在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 上构建一个自我改进的智能体式智能文档处理系统，其中八个专业智能体在两个基于图的工作流中协作，部署通常不到 20 分钟。文章引用 IDC 研究称，文档挑战每年给每位信息工作者造成 $19,732 的损失，并将生产率降低 21.3%；员工可能将多达 30% 的时间花在文档任务上；人工数据录入错误率在 1–4% 之间。

news.title: Generate presentations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS 描述了使用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 和 Strands Agents 框架构建一个生成 PowerPoint 演示文稿的 supervisor agent，内部测试中不到 90 秒即可完成。该方案使用 Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6、Amazon Titan Text Embeddings v2 和 Stability AI Stable Image Inpaint，通过基于 .NET 8 minimal API 构建的 REST API 暴露 generate_pptx 和 generate_summary 工具，并将向量存储在 Amazon OpenSearch Serverless 中。

news.title: How Tamnoon built AI-powered cloud security remediation with Amazon Bedrock
